complete_current_proof1_1: 1.1 Choose the ordered orthonormal basis of [F3]. In its coordinates $q(u)=\langle Mu,u\rangle$ is a real continuous quadratic polynomial, bounded on the unit sphere by the finite sum of the absolute matrix entries. By [F4], enumerate all rational-coordinate vectors $y_k\in(\mathbb Q+i\mathbb Q)^D$, and put $v_k=y_k/\|y_k\|$ when $y_k\ne0$ and $v_k=e_1$ otherwise. For any unit $x$ and $\varepsilon>0$, coordinatewise rational approximation gives $\|y-x\|<\min(\varepsilon/2,1/2)$ for such a $y$. Then $y\ne0$ and the reverse triangle inequality gives $\|y/\|y\|-x\|\le|1-\|y\||+\|y-x\|\le2\|y-x\|<\varepsilon$. Thus the $v_k$ are dense on the sphere; they are normalizations of rational-coordinate vectors, not necessarily rational-coordinate vectors themselves. Let $m=\sup_{\|u\|=1}q(u)$. For each $n\ge1$ take the least index $k(n)$ with $q(v_{k(n)})>m-1/n$, which exists by continuity and density. This deterministic rule uses no countable choice. By [F1] the bounded sequence $v_{k(n)}$ has a convergent subsequence; its limit has norm one and attains $m$. [given, F1, F2, F3, F4, construct]

The Cauchy-sequence reals $\mathbb{R}_C$ have the **least-upper-bound property**:
every nonempty $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}_C$ that is bounded above has a least upper
bound $\sup S \in \mathbb{R}_C$. Hence, together with [[thm-reals-ordered-field]],
$\mathbb{R}_C$ is a **complete ordered field** ([[def-complete-ordered-field]]).
